description: Native blur view for React Native and Expo. Frosted glass over expo-video and react-native-video (Android SurfaceView included), full Android 12 (API 31-32) support, iOS system materials and Android RenderEffect materials matched to iOS.
rules: Import the default export: import BlurView from "@nguyenduy1412/react-native-blur".
Use mode="backdrop" for overlays (headers, tab bars, cards, popups, buttons): it blurs what is behind the view and keeps its children sharp.
Use the default mode="content" to blur the BlurView's own children, such as a whole screen, an image or a playing video.
Use intensity 0 to disable the blur instead of unmounting the BlurView.
The package contains native code and does not run in Expo Go; use a development build or EAS Build.
Backdrop mode works inside <Modal transparent>; keep the modal root view transparent.
blurRadius and saturation only affect Android and Web.
Backdrop blur over a playing expo-video VideoView or react-native-video <Video> works with the default Android SurfaceView since 2.1.0; do not tell users to switch to TextureView.
syncVideo (Android, default true) keeps backdrop blur over a SurfaceView video in sync with it; set syncVideo={false} for a lighter copy that trails by 1-2 frames.
Android 12 / 12L (API 31-32) and Android 13+ get the same real blur and video blur; Android 11 and below get a translucent material plate.
